newsitem.title: USA: American General sees ratings revised.
newsitem.headline: American General sees ratings revised.

text.p: American General Corp said it expects the rating agencies to revise certain of its and its subsidiaries' debt, preferred and/or claims-paying ability ratings as a result of its agreement to buy USLIFE Corp.
The company did not say whether it expects the ratings to be lowered and a spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
However, in its statement, American General said it remains committed to its strategy of internal growth and growth through acquisitions.

"While we acknowledge the rating agencies' changing guidelines, American General is taking the necessary actions to build a stronger organization and we expect to continue to pursue strategic opportunities resulting from ongoing industry consolidation," American General chief executive Robert Devlin said.

Devlin said its actions come as the financial services industry undergoes a period of unprecedented consolidation, which he said will reduce the number of providers of financial products and services.
"The remaining providers will be financially stronger and more capable of meeting the changing needs of their many constituents," he said.
American General said its targeted capital structure consists of a minimum of 60 percent common equity, 15 percent preferred equity and a maximum of 25 percent debt.

American General said the USLIFE acquisition is an important transaction in its growth strategy, noting that it will position the company as the third largest writer of new individual life insurance premium in the nation.
American General said it has demonstrated its ability to successfully acquire and consolidate companies into its operations.
Over the past 20 years, the company said, it has completed 23 acquisitions totaling $6.5 billion and 24 divestitures totaling $2.0 billion.
